findings.element: Change plan & add-ons drawer → "Review & confirm" button, then toast "Plan updated… prorated credit applied"
findings.finding: The button promises a review step, but pressing it closes the drawer and announces the change as done. There is never a screen telling me what will be charged to my card today, and the word "prorated credit" appears for the first time *after* the money decision is made.
findings.user_impact: I press a button labelled "Review", expect a summary, and instead get "Plan updated". I don't know if my card was just charged $220, $1,104, or nothing. That is the moment I'd stop touching this page and email support — or my accountant.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the actual review step: "You'll be charged $X today. Your next charge is $Y on 27 Jul 2027." Say "the months you already paid for are taken off this price" instead of "prorated credit", and only then show a Confirm button.

findings.element: Sync balance card → "Autocharge when depleted" toggle
findings.finding: A toggle that lets Synder charge my card automatically, with no amount, no rate, and no ceiling anywhere near it. "Depleted" is also not a word I'd use — I'd have to guess it means "used up".
findings.user_impact: This is the single control on the page that can take money without me being there. With no maximum shown, I leave it off — and then my syncing silently pauses in a busy month, which is the outcome the toggle exists to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to "Keep syncing if I run out — charge me automatically", state the rate and a monthly cap next to it ("$15 per 500 extra transactions, never more than $X/month"), and let me set the cap.

findings.element: Add-ons list → "Invoicing" and "Smart rules" quantity steppers
findings.finding: These are sold to me as bare numbers. The stepper shows "Invoicing: 20" and "Smart rules: 3" with no unit — 20 invoices? 20 batches? 20 customers? "Flat fee per invoice batch instead of a commission" assumes I know what Synder charges a commission on today.
findings.user_impact: I can't tell what I'd get for the money, so I don't buy it and I don't know whether I'm missing something I need. If I do buy, I have no idea whether 20 is enough for my volume.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the unit in the number ("Invoicing — up to 20 invoices per month") and describe the outcome in my words: "Send invoices from Synder for one flat monthly fee instead of a percentage of each invoice."

findings.element: Bottom bar → "Confirm changes" (help text: "nothing is charged until you confirm")
findings.finding: The reassurance says nothing is charged until I confirm — which correctly tells me that confirming *is* the charge. But the bar only shows a monthly figure ($220/mo) and "unused balance is credited". It never shows the amount that hits my card, and pressing Confirm applies everything immediately with no summary.
findings.user_impact: I'm on a yearly plan. The bar says $220/mo, so am I about to be charged $220 or $2,640? I would not press that button without knowing, and there is nowhere on the page to find out.
findings.suggested_fix: Make Confirm open a one-screen summary: today's charge in dollars, the next charge and its date, and what happens to the money I already paid. Keep the running monthly total in the bar as the preview.

findings.element: Plan comparison matrix → quantity rows across Essential / Pro / Premium columns
findings.finding: One big table where the same row shows a stepper in one column and grey "included" text in the others, and the Premium column shows the word "negotiated" where a price should be. I can't tell which numbers describe what I have now, what I'd get, or what I'd pay.
findings.user_impact: The table is the whole page, and it's the part I understand least. "negotiated" is not a price — it reads like the answer is being withheld from me. I'd stop and go look at the public pricing page instead, which is where I'd start comparing competitors.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark my current column clearly ("You have this today"), grey the others as "what you'd get", and replace "negotiated" with "We agree a price with you — talk to us".

findings.element: "Sync balance" / "Historical transactions" tiles in the Billing column
findings.finding: Two separate pools of transactions with no explanation of how they relate: a monthly "Sync balance" of 1,000 and a "Historical transactions" pool of 0 "for back-dated syncs once the monthly balance is empty". The autocharge toggle sits under one of them with no amount.
findings.user_impact: I sell on Shopify and Amazon and I import last quarter's sales all the time. I can't work out which bucket that comes out of, whether I'll run dry mid-import, or what it costs when I do. Getting that wrong feels like it breaks my books, so I don't try.
findings.suggested_fix: Show one plain sentence: "This month: 1,000 left. Importing anything dated before <date> uses your historical pool (0 left, $30 per 1,000)." Put the autocharge rate and cap in the same tile.

findings.element: "Billing help" card → Cancel subscription (inside a panel titled "Coupons, custom plans, common questions, and cancelling")
findings.finding: Cancelling lives behind a card called "Billing help", together with coupons and FAQs. Nothing on the 9-card overview says "subscription" or "cancel".
findings.user_impact: When I want out, I want out in thirty seconds. Hunting through nine cards and finding it filed under "help" reads as deliberate — that's the point where I stop trusting the company, not just the screen, and I'd charge back rather than search again.
findings.suggested_fix: Put "Cancel subscription" at the bottom of the Plan & add-ons card where I'd look for it, and leave the coupon/FAQ card for help.

findings.element: Sync balance panel → "Autocharge when the balance runs out — You're charged per block of transactions at your plan's rate"
findings.finding: This is the clearest autocharge explanation of the four Round-2 prototypes and it still contains no number. "Per block" and "your plan's rate" are things I'd have to go and look up, and there's no maximum.
findings.user_impact: An automatic charge with an unstated rate and no ceiling is exactly the thing I've been burned by before. I leave it off, then get caught out in December when my volume triples.
findings.suggested_fix: Fill in the numbers inline — "$15 per 500 extra transactions" — and add a cap I set myself: "Never charge more than $__ in a month."

findings.element: Pending changes basket → "Confirm everything" (footer shows e.g. "$220.00 /mo · $30.00 one-time")
findings.finding: The basket is genuinely reassuring — "Nothing has been charged or saved yet" is the best sentence in any of these prototypes. But one button then applies a plan change, a real one-time purchase and an address edit together, and nothing says when each hits my card.
findings.user_impact: I hesitate before the last click because I've bundled a $30 purchase with an address change, and I can't tell if the $30 is charged now or added to next year's invoice. I'd probably empty the basket and do things one at a time — which loses the whole benefit of the design.
findings.suggested_fix: In the basket, timestamp each line: "$30.00 — charged to ••••4242 today", "Plan change — from your next invoice, 27 Jul 2027", "Address — saved immediately, no charge".

findings.element: Usage insight card ("You're using about 35% of your transaction allowance… See a smaller option") → confirm screen ("Remaining balance you would lose (not refundable) $1,012.00")
findings.finding: The page tells me I'm overpaying and gives me a button to fix it. Following that button lands on a screen saying the fix costs me a thousand dollars I can't get back.
findings.user_impact: It feels like being invited into a trap. The advice was right and the honesty on the second screen is right, but the sequence makes me angry at Synder rather than grateful — and the safe answer (wait for renewal) was available before I ever clicked.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the insight card offer the outcome that doesn't cost money: "You could pay $X less from 27 Jul 2027 — schedule it now, nothing wasted", with "change immediately instead" as the secondary path.

findings.element: Review-change modal footer → "Downgrade now anyway (lose $1,012.00)" vs "Schedule it for 27 Jul 2027 instead" placed in the body text
findings.finding: The expensive, irreversible option sits in the footer where every other screen puts the action you're meant to press. The option that loses me nothing is a link inside a paragraph above it.
findings.user_impact: I read footers as "the way forward". Under time pressure I'd click the footer button — the label does say I'm losing money, but I've already decided the footer is the way out of the dialog.
findings.suggested_fix: Make "Schedule for 27 Jul 2027 — you lose nothing" the primary footer button, and demote "Downgrade now and forfeit $1,012.00" to a plain text link.

findings.element: Right rail → "Autocharge when depleted / Keeps syncing past your allowance instead of pausing"; add-on rows marked "≈"
findings.finding: The best-explained autocharge of the set still shows no rate and no ceiling. Separately, two of the four things I can buy have a "≈" symbol next to their price with no explanation of what approximate means when it's my money.
findings.user_impact: Everything else on this page tells me exactly what happens to my money, which is why these two gaps stand out. "About this much" next to a price makes me want the real number before I commit.
findings.suggested_fix: State the autocharge rate and let me set a monthly maximum. Either resolve the "≈" prices to real ones or say plainly "final price shown before you confirm".

findings.element: Add-ons → "Revenue recognition — Turns raw transactions into ASC-606-compliant revenue, deferred and recognized over time", billed as "up to 1,000 recognition events — $79/mo"
findings.finding: Four terms I don't know in one sentence: ASC-606, compliant, deferred, recognized over time. It's then priced by "recognition events", a unit I have no way to count for my own business.
findings.user_impact: $79/mo is real money and this row is the biggest single line on my invoice after the plan. I can't tell whether I need it, whether I'm already over 1,000 events, or what happens if I am. I'd cancel it out of caution — or never buy it and never know I needed it.
findings.suggested_fix: Lead with who it's for and what it does: "If you sell subscriptions, this spreads the money across the months you earn it, the way your accountant needs it for year-end." Price it in something I can count, or show my current count next to the limit.

findings.element: Danger zone → "Cancel subscription — All add-ons including RevRec stop… We keep your data for 90 days"
findings.finding: "We keep your data for 90 days" tells me my data is deleted on day 91. Nothing says what happens to the sales already posted into QuickBooks, and the section is headed "Danger zone".
findings.user_impact: I keep my books for tax reasons — my accountant needs seven years, not ninety days. Read literally, cancelling destroys my records, so I would not cancel here; I'd cancel the card at my bank instead, which is worse for both of us.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate the two things explicitly: "Everything Synder already posted to QuickBooks stays in QuickBooks — it's yours. Your Synder history stays readable for 90 days after cancelling." Drop "Danger zone" for "Ending your subscription".

findings.element: Header strip → "mid-cycle changes are adjusted fairly and shown inline"
findings.finding: "Adjusted fairly" is a promise with no number behind it, and "mid-cycle" and "inline" are both words I'd have to decode.
findings.user_impact: It's the one sentence on the page about what changing my plan costs, and it tells me nothing. "Fairly" by whose reckoning? I assume the worst and don't change anything until my renewal — or I ask my accountant to do it, which means I never learn the tool.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with the arithmetic: "Change your plan today and we take the months you've already paid for off the new price. You'll see the exact amount before you confirm."

findings.element: Subscription section → "New total: $92.00/mo" + "Apply changes"
findings.finding: The only thing between me and a billing change is a button called "Apply changes" and a monthly figure. Nothing says whether Apply charges my card, changes my next invoice, or takes effect at renewal — and there's no "nothing is charged yet" anywhere on the page.
findings.user_impact: "Apply" sounds harmless, like saving a preference, so I'd press it while I was still exploring — and then spend the next ten minutes hunting for whether I'd just spent money. That's the exact feeling that made me abandon my last two tools.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to "Review new price", and open a confirmation stating the dollar amount charged today, the date of the next charge, and "nothing has been charged yet".

findings.element: Subscription card → "Cancel subscription" link
findings.finding: A plain cancel link sitting beside "Upgrade plan" and "Download invoices", with no statement of what cancelling does to my syncing, my data, or the year I've already paid for.
findings.user_impact: It's one stray click away from "Change payment method", and I have no idea whether pressing it stops my books tonight or at renewal. I avoid that whole cluster of buttons — including the ones I actually needed.
findings.suggested_fix: Move it away from the routine actions and put the consequences in the confirmation: what keeps working, until when, what happens to data, and that reactivating is one click.

findings.element: "Autocharge when sync balance is depleted" toggle; Notifications → "Get reminded when transactions need reconciliation"; Historical transactions → "Get 50 free"
findings.finding: Three unexplained terms in the words themselves: "sync balance is depleted", "reconciliation", and a "Get 50 free" button with no explanation of what I have to do to earn them. The stepper tooltips ($10 per 500, $7 per user) are the one place this page explains money well — the same care isn't applied to these.
findings.user_impact: "Reconciliation" is the word my accountant uses and I nod along to. Being asked to configure reminders about it makes me feel like this software is for them, not me, and "Get 50 free" next to "Purchase" makes me suspect a catch.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "reminder to check your Synder records against your bank and platform each month". Say "when this month's transactions run out". Change "Get 50 free" to "Earn 50 free by referring Synder".

findings.element: "Autocharge when sync balance runs out" — shown already set to "On", with only an "i" icon
findings.finding: Permission to charge my card automatically is switched on by default, with no rate, no cap, and no sentence explaining it — just an information icon.
findings.user_impact: This is the thing I'm most afraid of: money leaving my account without me pressing anything. Finding it already enabled, on my behalf, with no limit, is worse than finding it off. I'd turn it off in reflex and lose the protection it was meant to give me.
findings.suggested_fix: Default it off, or default it on with a visible ceiling and rate spelled out in the row: "On — up to $__ /month, at $15 per 500 extra transactions. Change limit."

findings.element: Plan ladder "Starter · Essential · Medium · Scale · Enterprise" above "Upgrade plan →"
findings.finding: Five tier names, no prices, no differences, no indication of what changes if I move one step. "Medium" and "Scale" don't tell me anything about size or cost.
findings.user_impact: I came here to find out whether a bigger plan would solve my problem. The one element that should answer that gives me five words and a link. I'd open the marketing site in a new tab — and once I'm comparing prices on a website, I'm comparing competitors too.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the price and the one number that matters per tier ("Medium — $220/mo, 10,000 transactions"), and mark which one I'm on.

findings.element: "Your plan includes: 1,000 transactions included" vs "Adjust your plan → Monthly transactions: 500 included in plan"
findings.finding: The same page states two different amounts for the thing I'm buying — 1,000 in the breakdown, 500 next to the stepper.
findings.user_impact: I can't tell how many transactions I actually have, so I can't tell whether I'm about to run out or about to overpay. Once a billing screen contradicts itself in front of me, I stop believing the total at the bottom too.
findings.suggested_fix: One number, one place — show "1,000 included in your plan" beside the stepper and have the stepper start from it.

findings.element: Add-ons row → clickable "Invoicing +$12/mo", "Smart Rules +$8/mo", "Historical Sync +$20/mo" cards (Smart Rules already highlighted as on)
findings.finding: Clicking anywhere on an add-on card switches a paid subscription on and instantly changes the total, with no confirmation and no undo shown. One of them is already active without my having bought it in this session.
findings.user_impact: I click things to find out what they are — that's how I explore software. Here, exploring signs me up. And because Smart Rules is already lit up, I can't tell what I'm paying for now versus what I've just added by looking around.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the whole card open a description; put a separate "Add — $8/mo" button inside it. Label the active one "Included in what you pay today" and require a confirm step for anything that changes the price.

findings.element: Subscription panel → "Autocharge — Automatically charge your card on the renewal date" toggle
findings.finding: Here autocharge means something different from every other prototype — it's about the renewal charge, not about running out of transactions. Nothing says what happens if I switch it off.
findings.user_impact: Turning it off might mean "don't take my money automatically" or might mean "your subscription lapses and syncing stops". Those are opposite outcomes and I can't tell which, so I don't touch it — and I still don't know whether money is coming out on the renewal date.
findings.suggested_fix: Spell out both branches: "On — we charge ••••4242 $1,104 on 13 Mar 2027. Off — we email you an invoice to pay manually; syncing pauses if it isn't paid by the renewal date."

findings.element: Subscription panel → "Cancel subscription" button, beside "Upgrade plan / Change card / Get invoices"; "Monthly limits" steppers
findings.finding: Cancel sits in the same button row as three routine actions, with no consequence text anywhere. Separately, the steppers I buy transactions and seats with are headed "Monthly limits", which sounds like a safety setting rather than a purchase.
findings.user_impact: The most irreversible button on the screen looks exactly like the harmless ones. And because "limits" sounds protective, I'd raise it thinking I was setting a ceiling and instead commit to a higher bill.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate cancel visually and put the consequences in its confirmation. Rename "Monthly limits" to "What you're buying each month" and mark included versus extra.

findings.element: Subscription table rows: "Pro plan", "Smart rules 3/10", "Invoicing 40/100", "RevRec 800/1,000", "Sales volume 10,000/20,000", "JS modes 2/3", "Users 2/3" — every row 20% and "95 USD/mo"
findings.finding: This is the list of what I'm paying for, and it's unreadable. "JS modes" and "RevRec" mean nothing to me, and all seven rows show the identical price of 95 USD/mo, which cannot be right. There is no total anywhere on the page.
findings.user_impact: I came to find out what I'm paying and why. Seven identical prices for seven different things, one of which I can't even name, tells me the billing screen is broken. If I can't trust the bill, I can't trust the numbers this thing writes into my books — and that is the whole reason I bought it.
findings.suggested_fix: Real per-line prices and a total row. Expand "RevRec" to "Revenue recognition" with one plain sentence, and either name "JS modes" in words a customer would recognise or remove it from the customer-facing bill.

findings.element: Cancel dialog → "your account will be downgraded to the free plan"
findings.finding: The cancel confirmation promises a free plan. Nothing anywhere else in the product mentions a free plan, and the other prototypes say syncing stops entirely.
findings.user_impact: I'd cancel believing my sales keep flowing into QuickBooks on a free tier. If that's wrong, I find out weeks later with a gap in my books at exactly the moment I'm doing my taxes. If it's right, nobody told me it existed before I tried to leave.
findings.suggested_fix: State what actually survives: "Syncing stops on <date>. What's already in QuickBooks stays there. Your Synder history stays readable. Nothing is deleted."

findings.element: "Add more" cards — Invoicing, RevRec, Smart rules all priced "from 99 USD per 100 invoices"
findings.finding: Three different products share one price unit, and it's the wrong unit for two of them — Smart rules and revenue recognition are not measured in invoices. Historical data is "per 100 transactions" with no indication of what I've used.
findings.user_impact: I cannot estimate what any of these would cost me, so I don't buy any of them. Worse, the copy-paste pricing makes me think nobody checked this page, which makes me doubt the invoice too.
findings.suggested_fix: One correct unit per product, plus my current usage against it ("Smart rules — $19.99 for up to 3 rules; you have 0").

findings.element: Add-on cards → price reads "$0.00 USD" next to an "Add" button, for all five add-ons
findings.finding: Every paid add-on displays $0.00 until after I commit — picking "Up to 200 invoices — $199.00" from the dropdown leaves the price showing $0.00 USD, and the only way forward is a button called "Add".
findings.user_impact: I would either press Add believing it's free, or refuse to press it because a $0.00 price next to a purchase button is obviously wrong. Both are bad: one is an accidental charge, the other is me closing the tab. This is the clearest "I might be charged by accident" moment in all eleven.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the selected tier's real price the moment it's chosen, and change "Add" to "Add for $199.00/mo" with a confirmation stating what's charged today.

findings.element: All five add-on descriptions: "Benefit from flat fee rather than commission on every invoice amount!" on Monthly transactions, Invoicing, Smart rules, Revenue recognition and Historical transactions
findings.finding: The same sentence describes five unrelated products, and it only makes sense for one of them. "Commission on every invoice amount" also implies Synder is currently taking a cut of my sales, which is news to me.
findings.user_impact: I learn nothing about any of them and pick up a false worry that I'm being charged commission on my revenue. I'd go and check my last invoice line by line instead of buying anything.
findings.suggested_fix: One outcome-first sentence each, in my language: what it does for my business, and the number it's measured in.

findings.element: "Monthly transactions" stepper starting at 500, and the header chip "Syncs left: 1000"
findings.finding: The stepper starts at 500 with no indication of what my plan already includes, while the header says I have 1,000 "syncs" left. Two numbers, two different words, and no relationship shown between them.
findings.user_impact: I don't know whether pressing + buys my 501st transaction or my 1,001st, so I can't tell what the extra costs. And "syncs" versus "transactions" makes me wonder if they're even the same thing being counted.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the stepper at what's included ("1,000 included in your plan — add more from here"), and use one word, transactions, everywhere including the header.

findings.element: Add-on cards in the "Plan and billing" section → "$0.00 USD" beside every "Add" button
findings.finding: Same as the tabbed version: the price stays $0.00 no matter which paid tier I select, and the commit button is simply "Add". On the long page this sits in the middle of a continuous scroll rather than behind a deliberate tab click.
findings.user_impact: On one long page I'm scrolling past these on my way to the org name field. A $0.00 purchase button in my scroll path is how I buy something by accident and only find out on the invoice.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the real selected price before Add, label the button with the amount, and confirm what will be charged today.

findings.element: One continuous page mixing free settings (organization name, time zone, notifications) with paid actions (add-on "Add" buttons, "Upgrade your plan", "Cancel subscription")
findings.finding: Nothing visually or verbally separates the controls that cost money from the ones that don't, and there is no running total or "nothing is charged yet" anywhere on the page. Notifications save silently on change; add-ons charge on click; both look the same.
findings.user_impact: I can't tell which parts of this page are safe to poke at. Since some of it takes money instantly, I treat the whole page as dangerous and only change things when someone tells me to — which means I never find the settings that would have helped me.
findings.suggested_fix: Group everything billable into one clearly-labelled money area with a single running total and confirm step; leave free preferences elsewhere with a visible "saved" marker.

findings.element: "Plan and billing" header → "Medium · Active · $79.99/month billed yearly · Next billing date 11/06/2021", above "Upgrade your plan"
findings.finding: The plan is called "Medium", which tells me nothing about size or what's above it; the price is monthly but billed yearly with no yearly figure shown; and the next billing date is in the past.
findings.user_impact: The three facts I most need — what I have, what it costs me in one payment, and when the money leaves — are the three I can't get. A billing date years in the past makes me think the page isn't showing my real account, so I stop reading it and email support.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the tier with its size ("Medium — 3,000 transactions/month"), both figures ("$79.99/mo, charged as $959.88 once a year"), and a real next-charge date.

ranking.why: It's the only one that tells me, in dollars, what happens to money I've already paid, stops me making a change that would lock people out, and promises out loud that nothing gets deleted.
"Nothing has been charged or saved yet" plus a basket I confirm once is the design that lets me poke around without fear — I just can't find the cancel button.
The total and the "+$X more per month" are always in front of me, so I always know which direction my bill is moving, even if I never learn what today's charge is.
The line-by-line "What you're paying for" table is the clearest explanation of my current bill anywhere, but the button that changes it skips the review it promises.
The Calm Overview's "Capped at $500/month — no surprise charges above this" is the single most reassuring sentence in this whole set; the ASC-606 copy and the 90-day data line undo it.
The stepper tooltips actually tell me what an extra 500 transactions costs before I commit, which no other Round 1 screen does — but "Apply changes" leaves me guessing whether my card was hit.
Autocharge already switched on with no ceiling, plus the page telling me I have 1,000 transactions in one place and 500 in another — I'd stop trusting the total.
The health cards at the top are genuinely calming, and then the add-on tiles sign me up for a paid feature on a single exploratory click.
Five add-ons, one copy-pasted description, and a $0.00 price on every purchase button — at least the paid section is behind its own tab.
Same $0.00 purchase buttons as the tabbed version, but now sitting in my scroll path between the org name field and the notification toggles.
Seven different things all priced at exactly 95 USD/mo, a line item called "JS modes", no total, and a cancel dialog that invents a free plan — I'd assume the billing is broken and leave.

verdict: v2 is the only one of the eleven I would not abandon: it is the single screen that answers the question I actually have — "if I press this, what leaves my bank account, and can I undo it?" — and it answers it in dollars, blocks me from a change that would quietly lock a colleague out, and states plainly that nothing gets deleted. C is close behind purely on the strength of "Nothing has been charged or saved yet." The scariest thing across all eleven is autocharge: in every prototype it is a switch that lets Synder take money from my card with no rate shown and no maximum I can set, and in V2 Billing Hub it is already switched on for me — Round 1's Calm Overview had solved this with "Capped at $500/month — no surprise charges above this", and not one Round 2 prototype carried that cap forward.
